timeline: 2025-08-12 — Inbound from PLG signups: API key created; initial usage was embeddings + short-form chat completions. (Self-serve)
2025-08-15 — Discovery call: current vendor is 'piecemeal' across teams; wants a single inference layer + better cost visibility. Notes: "We can’t get Finance comfortable with per-token surprises."
2025-08-20 — Shared hosted quickstart + suggested guardrails (rate limits, quotas, per-route budgets). Introduced Dedicated as the predictable-throughput upgrade path.

2025-08-26 — Live demo (standard tenant): ran Hosted quickstart first (streaming chat), then pivoted to Dedicated story (reserved capacity + isolation) and showed Console cost/latency breakdown. Prospect asked to avoid hard pricing numbers on the call.
2025-08-28 — Follow-up: sent security FAQ + demo quickstart links; agreed to define a 2-week evaluation plan with success metrics (p95 latency, cost per resolved ticket, fallback behavior).
2025-09-03 — Pricing alignment chat: wants ballpark ranges + commitment options; asked if Dedicated can start small and scale. Flagged procurement involvement if spend > $150k/yr.
notes:
Account context / PLG -> sales:
- Vectra team started via PLG (devs building an internal support-agent + summarization feature set). Usage is growing beyond one team; now central platform group is involved.
- Primary pain: unpredictable spend + lack of visibility per feature. Quote from discovery: "Our PMs ship prompts weekly; we need guardrails and fast rollback when quality or cost regresses."

What we showed / what landed:
- Started with Hosted API quickstart (curl/SDK style) to match how they already onboard.
- Emphasized Console observability: token cost breakdown, latency histograms, per-route dashboards.
- Dedicated upgrade path resonated: "We need to tell leadership we can buy capacity and isolate noisy neighbors." They asked specifically about how Dedicated changes throttling/429 behavior and whether burst is possible.

Technical notes (light / from SE):
- Workload mix: 60% summarization (tickets/cases), 30% retrieval-augmented QA over KB, 10% internal tooling / ad hoc.
- Latency target stated on call: p95 < 800ms for short responses; streaming acceptable for longer outputs.
- Wants a defined fallback story: if primary model is degraded, route to compatible variant (quality tradeoff is OK if communicated).

Security/compliance:
- Not heavily regulated, but enterprise customers are asking them about SOC2 posture end-to-end.
- Requests: SSO/SAML for console access, audit logs for admin changes, retention controls (don’t keep prompts forever).
- No hard requirement for VPC/on-prem at this stage; they asked if Dedicated implies isolation (answered yes for compute pool + data isolation posture, with Private/VPC as future option if needed).

Pricing / procurement:
- Very pricing sensitive; specifically asked us not to show $/1M token numbers in shared decks. Comfortable with ranges and committing once usage is forecastable.
- Concern: cost spikes from prompt changes; wants budgeting controls + alerting.

Next steps (proposed by AE):
1) Run a scoped Hosted evaluation with 2-3 fixed prompt sets + expected outputs.
2) In parallel, do Dedicated sizing call (peak TPS + context lengths + concurrency); provide a dedicated starting configuration + scale plan.
3) Define the "upgrade gate" criteria: when their usage or SLOs require Dedicated.

Risks / watchouts:
- If we can’t articulate a clean narrative for cost predictability (especially during prompt iteration), they may revert to an in-house vLLM deployment for cost control.
- Need to be careful on benchmarks/claims: keep to approved ranges, emphasize observability and knobs.

Internal links/stubs:
- Demo deck + talk track: see linked Drive docs.
- Support reference: SUP-18411 (prior confusion about 429 throttling in a trial context; use this as a caution for setting demo-safe defaults and explaining quotas early).
